    Track 3 · With BrewSLM · Lesson 1

    From script to platform: the BrewSLM lifecycle

    After this lesson you can map your by-hand script onto BrewSLM's eleven-stage lifecycle and explain what the platform adds: per-row accountability, pass/fail rules, and an auditable RunEvent stream.

    Level: intermediate Read time: ~9 min Prerequisites: Experiment tracking with MLflow & W&B (Track 2) Verified: 12 Nov 2026

    In the Track 2 capstone you wrote a single script: load a model, build and tokenize data, train a LoRA adapter, evaluate against a baseline, and ship. That script works — and now you understand every line of it. Track 3 takes that same pipeline and runs it through BrewSLM, so you can see exactly which platform surface stands in for each thing you did by hand, and what it buys you when you do this not once but fifty times.

    The eleven-stage lifecycle

    Your script had a handful of phases. This track teaches the BrewSLM flow as eleven explicit stages, each with declared inputs, outputs and a contract — no mystery boxes. The eleven stages are a teaching model of the lifecycle, not eleven services:

    01 Ingest        →  pull rows from a source
02 Introspect    →  guess the data's shape
03 Map (dry-run) →  preview the mapping + rejections
04 Map (commit)  →  write mapped rows
05 Clean         →  (optional) PII, quality, chunks
06 Prepare       →  build the manifest + train/eval splits
07 Preflight     →  will this run? deps, capability, VRAM risk
08 Train         →  recipe + checkpoints + loss/eval traces
09 Evaluate      →  eval pack + pass/fail rules (PASS / FAIL)
10 Export        →  GGUF / ONNX / HF / TensorRT-LLM / Docker
11 Deploy        →  (optional) versioned endpoint + drift checks

    From Track 2

    Your script maps almost one-to-one: build-a-dataset → Ingest/Map (01–04); tokenize/collate + split → Prepare (06); the LoRA Trainer loop → Train (08); evaluate-by-hand → Evaluate (09); merge-and-ship → Export/Deploy (10–11). The new stages — Introspect, Preflight, Clean — are the safety rails you didn't write.

    In the workspace the eleven stages fold into the six destinations of a project's left sidebar (/project/<id>): Overview (where you are, the next step, the latest run, the shipped model), Data with five numbered steps — Sources (01–04), Prepare (05), Labels (the answer key), Generate (synthetic rows), Split (06) — Train (07–08: the readiness line is preflight, the form is the run), Results (09: Verdict / Failures / Compare / Try it), Ship (10–11: Package / Publish / Deploy / Monitor) and Settings. The rest of this track names those places as it goes.

    The RunEvent audit stream

    The single most important difference from a script is the audit spine. Import, training, evaluation, export and deployment (plus data annotation and distillation capture) write RunEvent rows via emit_event(), each with a severity (info / warning / error / critical) and, for error and critical events, a reason code from a taxonomy that emit_event() validates at runtime. Introspect, the mapping preview, Clean, Prepare and Preflight emit no RunEvent today. One stream feeds the run timeline and the failure clusters on Ship → Monitor, and the support bundle. When your by-hand script failed, you read a stack trace; when a BrewSLM run times out or can't be handed to the worker, it emits a named event (training_timeout, training_dispatch_error) that those views pick up automatically. (Other real-run failures don't reach the timeline today; they are recorded on the run itself, as a failure banner with the log tail. Lesson 3.7 shows it.)

    It starts with a project

    Everything in BrewSLM hangs off a project: a base model, its data, its recipes, its experiments, its deployments, and its event history. Where your script kept state in local files and variables, the project is the durable container that makes the pipeline resumable, auditable, and shareable. Create one with + New Project (a name and "What problem do you want this model to solve?") or open a starter project, and you land on its Overview — stage 01 is Data → Sources.

    Key idea

    BrewSLM isn't doing anything you didn't do by hand — it's doing the same pipeline with explicit contracts and an audit trail. You learned the internals first precisely so the platform is transparent, not magic. The rest of this track walks the eleven stages in order.

    Key terms

    BrewSLM lifecycle
    The eleven explicit stages from Ingest to Deploy, each with inputs, outputs and a contract; a teaching model of the flow.
    RunEvent
    An audit row (severity, plus a reason code on errors) written by import, training, evaluation, export and deploy; it feeds the run timeline and clusters on Ship → Monitor.
    project
    The durable container for a base model, its data, recipes, experiments, deployments, and event history.
    contract
    The declared guarantee of a stage — what it promises about its inputs and outputs.
